claim_text: Illinois DNR says staff spotted an “apparent cyberattack”, an attempt at unauthorized access, at the Algonquin Dam on Monday, Nov 16
summary: CBS quotes IDNR calling it an “apparent cyberattack”. ABC7 and Shaw Local say “attempt”. IDNR's Office of Water Resources, which runs the dam, spotted it.
detail: The word “apparent” is the state's own. No outlet says how it was detected or what was targeted. We could not find the IDNR release on a state website, so we rely on outlets that quote or paraphrase it. The Chicago Tribune, the first outlet to report it, calls it an “attempted cyberattack” but opens by saying the dam “was subject to a cyberattack”, which is stronger than IDNR's wording. A link-aggregator post titled this “hacked”, which is also stronger.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Five outlets relay IDNR's own description, which is hedged (“apparent”). The attack is not independently shown.
notes: Not marked Confirmed: the state itself says “apparent” and gives no technical detail.

claim_text: IDNR announced the incident on Friday, Nov 20, and named four agencies helping
summary: The Chicago Tribune and Shaw Local say IDNR announced it in a news release Friday; CBS, ABC7 and Gizmodo carry the same statement. Helping: Illinois State Police, IEMA, Illinois DoIT and the federal CISA.
detail: Several independent outlets carry the same statement, and the Tribune and Shaw Local quote the release. We did not read the release itself. We found no separate statement from CISA or the state police.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Independent outlets in different newsrooms agree that IDNR made this statement.

claim_text: IDNR says staff blocked unauthorized access and the dam kept operating
summary: CBS says staff “immediately took action to prevent any unauthorized access and keep the dam running”. ABC7 and Shaw Local quote the dam as kept “secure and fully operational”.
detail: This is the agency's own account. Nobody outside IDNR has checked it, and officials gave no detail on whether any system was reached.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Several outlets relay IDNR's statement; no independent check.

claim_text: State and federal agencies are investigating
summary: CBS, ABC7, Shaw Local and Gizmodo say Illinois State Police, IEMA, Illinois DoIT and CISA are involved with IDNR.
detail: We found no CISA statement of its own. CISA's involvement comes from IDNR's account.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: All four relay IDNR; CISA has not been heard from directly.

claim_text: IDNR says it has no indication the incident is connected to other recent cyber events or nationwide outages
summary: CBS says IDNR had no indication of a link to nationwide outages. The Chicago Tribune and Shaw Local quote the release: IDNR has “no indication at this time” that the incident is related to other cyber events.
detail: This is what IDNR said, and several outlets agree. It is a statement of no indication, not proof there is no link.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Independent outlets agree on what IDNR said; Shaw Local quotes the release.
notes: The claim is about the statement, not the underlying question; see c006.

claim_text: The Algonquin Dam incident is part of the wave of outages and attacks in recent weeks
summary: No source ties it to the Microsoft 365, FAA, bank-app or other outages. Gizmodo sees no reason to suspect a link beyond loose timing. The White House's Nov 18 release does not mention the dam.
detail: Absence of evidence is not a finding. Investigators have not published conclusions.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: IDNR says it has no indication of a link and no source shows one.

claim_text: Who was behind it, and how it was done
summary: Officials gave no information about the nature of the attack, its source, or the systems involved. Hindustan Times says they declined to comment on the suspected source, citing the investigation.
detail: No claim of responsibility has been reported, and we did not look for one on leak sites or underground forums.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source gives an actor, a method or a target.

claim_text: Attackers gained access to the dam's control or operating systems
summary: No source says this happened. IDNR says staff prevented unauthorized access. Whether any system was reached has not been said either way.
detail: A headline calling the dam “hacked” overstates what IDNR has said.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: IDNR describes access as prevented and gives no detail either way.

claim_text: The dam is small: about 9 feet high and 300 feet long, with a “Significant” hazard rating
summary: Gizmodo, citing the Dams of the World site, describes a concrete rockfill dam 9 ft high and 300 ft long, storing up to 24,200 acre-feet, rated “Significant” hazard (no probable loss of life, but possible economic or environmental damage).
detail: One outlet's figures from a database we did not read. Context only; it says nothing about what the attacker tried.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Single outlet relaying a third-party database.

claim_text: The White House said on Nov 18 it sees no indication of a cyberattack behind recent tech outages; it does not mention the dam
summary: A Nov 18 White House release quotes the DNI and the National Security Adviser saying they see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack and no evidence the recent incidents are related.
detail: The release predates IDNR's Nov 20 announcement and does not mention Algonquin Dam. It is context, not a finding about the dam.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The release is the primary source for what officials said.

claim_text: IDNR's Office of Water Resources runs the dam's hinged crest gate, which it uses to regulate Fox River flows and reduce flooding
summary: IDNR's public page on the Stratton and Algonquin Dams says the gates at both dams are operated under an operating guide to regulate flow downstream and reduce flooding along the Chain O'Lakes and the Fox River.
detail: Background on what the dam does. It says nothing about what the attacker tried or reached.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: IDNR's own page describes the hinged crest gate at Algonquin Dam and how the Office of Water Resources operates the gates.
